front.title: Stapled Merkle Revocation Proofs for Pseudonymous ITS Credentials (SMRP)

author.organization: Telecom Paris, Institut Polytechnique de Paris
Telecom Paris, Institut Polytechnique de Paris
Telecom Paris, Institut Polytechnique de Paris, and Institut CyberIA

abstract.t:
Pseudonymous Intelligent Transport Systems (ITS) credentials are short-lived and numerous. Verifiers decide at message-reception time, often without connectivity, which makes revocation status hard to deliver. This document specifies Stapled Merkle Revocation Proofs (SMRP). For each partition of a revocation domain, an authorized issuer signs a compact checkpoint that commits to the complete sorted set of revoked credential tokens. A credential holder staples a logarithmic-size proof that its token is absent from that set, and a verifier checks the proof offline against the current checkpoint. Freshness is carried by the checkpoint, which is public, shared by every credential of the partition, and deliverable by any party. Within one stream, a proof remains usable across checkpoints for as long as the set commitment is unchanged and the current checkpoint is admissible. The same commitment supports proofs of revocation that anyone can relay, complete authenticated lists for capable verifiers, and public audit.
The document defines a credential identity that does not depend on the certificate signature, a Merkle tree over the intervals of the sorted revoked set with one authentication path per proof, the checkpoint and staple encodings, conservative time validation with a conditional bound on the last affirmative decision after revocation, verifier state with terminal revocation, and carriage in V2X secured messages and in TLS 1.3. It positions SMRP against the companion pOCSP mechanism: pOCSP signs one statement per certificate and validity window, whereas SMRP signs one statement per partition and issuance period. This document is Experimental and allocates no identifier in ETSI, IEEE, or SAE namespaces.
